rationale: A dried-fig trial measured menstrual symptoms and perceived stress. A separate high-potassium case and fig mixture study give no hallucination-frequency estimate. The adult surgical series and juvenile levodopa case record visual hallucinations in different treatment settings. Dried fig effects on visual hallucination frequency in Parkinson disease remain unresolved.

A state-anxiety comparison favored a dried berry mixture with 16.7% raspberry over cocoa in an exploratory healthy-volunteer analysis. The frozen-fruit thesis measured oxidative biomarkers. The recovered isolated ketone paper assessed depression-like behavior in mice, and the human raspberry powder experiment has no separate anxiety estimate. The direction for frozen raspberry and Parkinson anxiety remains unresolved.

One Parkinson diet cohort recorded apathy and pooled dried fruit, and controlled diet research has no separate date contrast. The mixed fiber bar and pilot give no individual apathy result. Other clinical reports measure apathy during DBS or as a predictor of impulse-control behavior. The effect of eating dried dates on Parkinson apathy remains unresolved.

Fresh green kiwi yielded an imprecise change in self-rated waking alertness. The controlled breakfast study gives inconclusive choice reaction-time and Stroop results after previously frozen kiwi pulp, and the separate COMPASS registry lacks results. The new kiwi meal experiment measured pig brain bioamines. These outcomes leave the direction for raw kiwi and Parkinson attention impairment unresolved.
